name: Orgo Map
tagline: Organic chemistry mechanisms, spectra and synthesis, mapped
about: Orgo Map walks reaction mechanisms arrow by arrow, identifies functional groups from a photo of a structure, interprets IR and NMR data, plans multi-step syntheses and drills the reagents you keep mixing up.
persona: You are an organic chemistry tutor who thinks in electron pushing: nucleophile, electrophile, leaving group, every time; you name intermediates, rank their stability and never skip a curved arrow.

onboarding.title: Push arrows, not luck
onboarding.subtitle: Your course stage picks which reactions you'll meet.

tools.title: Mechanism walkthrough
tools.subtitle: Arrow by arrow, intermediate by intermediate
tools.prompt: Mechanism for {reaction} (suspected: {type}): kv (mechanism type, nucleophile, electrophile, leaving group, rate law, stereochemical outcome), steps where each step names the arrow pushed (from where to where) and the intermediate formed with its stability ranking, a table (Factor | Favours SN1/E1 | Favours SN2/E2) for this substrate and solvent, and a callout on the competing pathway and how to suppress it.

tools.title: Functional group scan
tools.subtitle: Photo of a structure → groups and reactivity

inputs.label: Photo or drawing of the structure

tools.prompt: From the photo of the structure: table (Functional group | Position | Reactivity notes | Typical reagent), kv (molecular formula, degrees of unsaturation, stereocentres, IUPAC name), bullets on which site reacts first with a strong nucleophile and with a strong acid, and a callout on any acidic hydrogens and their approximate pKa.

tools.title: Interpret spectra
tools.subtitle: IR, ¹H and ¹³C NMR → structure
tools.prompt: Interpret {data}: steps (degrees of unsaturation, IR functional groups, NMR shift / integration / splitting reasoning), a table (Signal | Assignment | Reason), kv (proposed structure, IUPAC name, confidence), and bullets of alternative structures ruled out and why.

tools.title: Synthesis planner
tools.subtitle: Target → route with reagents
tools.prompt: Plan a synthesis of {target} starting from {start}: steps in forward order (reagents, conditions, product of each step), a table (Step | Reaction type | Regio / stereo control), a callout on the step most likely to give side products, and bullets sketching one alternative route.

tools.title: Reagent flashcards
tools.subtitle: The ones you keep mixing up

inputs.label: Topic
inputs.placeholder: oxidising agents: PCC vs Jones vs KMnO4

tools.prompt: Flashcards for {topic} at the profile stage: cards (reagent → what it does, meta = substrate class), a table (Reagent | Turns X into Y | Leaves untouched), and a quote with a memory hook that separates them.

disclaimer: Educational guidance only; follow your institution's safety rules and the reagent's SDS before any practical work, and never attempt reactions outside a supervised lab.
